subject: 🏃 Thursday — 4 mi Easy (illness gate, Wk 4)
html:
Tomorrow's Rx: 4 mi easy @ 9:15–9:30 — but only if you pass the neck check. The cold you flagged yesterday morning is the binding constraint on everything this week, not the training plan. Before you lace up, run the checklist: (1) symptoms still above-the-neck only — no chest tightness, no deep cough, (2) no fever, (3) resting HR within 5 bpm of your baseline, (4) energy near-normal, (5) symptoms clearly improving, not just stable. All five must hold. Any miss → full rest, no run.

If you pass: 4 mi conversational pace on flat terrain (Bayfront or neighborhood), HR cap 145. Strides are dropped — the fast-twitch priming isn't worth the metabolic cost when your immune system is working. Pre-run: 5-min activation (hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges) + quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side). Wear the H10 — you need clean HR data to confirm the run stayed aerobic and to baseline your resting HR for the Friday-night race-day go/no-go call.

Focus cue: Listen to your body, not your ambition. If you start the run and anything feels off — elevated effort at easy pace, chest involvement, lightheadedness — walk home. A DNS Thursday costs nothing. A forced run that deepens the illness costs you Saturday's race and potentially weeks of training quality.

Context: Week 4 of 12, Phase 1 — PAL 10K is 2 days out. Friday is full rest regardless. Saturday's go/no-go gets made Friday night using the same five-point checklist plus a 24-hr fever-free requirement. The 10K is a calibration race, not a target race — Presidio HM in 3.5 weeks is the actual Pivot test. No scenario where forcing Saturday serves the marathon if you're still fighting this off.

Tonight: Hydrate aggressively, zinc + Vit C if you have them, bed by 9:30. Check your resting HR before you fall asleep and again when you wake up — that delta is the most honest signal you'll get tomorrow morning.
